items.title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
items.body:
Tool Retrieval is now in preview in the Gemini Interactions API. Load tool parameter schemas on demand instead of sending your full tool library in every prompt,designed to reduce input tokens and keep tool selection accurate as your agent scales.

Research Scientist, Google DeepMind

Your browser does not support the audio element.

We are launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API to help your agents manage large tool libraries more efficiently. By loading parameter schemas only when needed, you reduce latency and input token costs for complex tasks. You can try this feature today in the Interactions API by adding a tool_search tool and setting defer_loading to true in your requests.

We are launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API to help you manage large tool libraries.

This feature reduces input token counts and latency by loading parameter schemas only when needed.

You can enable this by adding a tool search and setting defer loading to true.

Tool Retrieval works with Gemini 3.6 and later models to support your complex agent tasks.

We are introducing Tool Retrieval to help developers manage large collections of software tools more efficiently. Instead of loading every tool at once, your agent now keeps a library on standby and only pulls in the specific details it needs for a task. This reduces data usage, speeds up performance, and improves accuracy. You can start using this feature today with our latest Gemini models to build more capable and responsive applications.

Today we're launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API, available in preview in the Interactions API.

When an agent connects to dozens or even hundreds of tools, sending every full parameter schema on every request adds up fast. It inflates input token counts, adds latency, and lowers tool-selection accuracy as the candidate list grows. Tool Retrieval lets your agent keep its full tool library on standby and load parameter schemas only when the current task needs them.

To turn on Tool Retrieval, add a tool_search tool to your request and set defer_loading: true on the tools you want to hold back. The model still sees the name and description of every deferred tool, so it knows what's available, but the parameter schemas stay out of context. When the model needs a tool, it asks for it by name, the API loads the full schema, and the model calls the function, all inside the same request.

from google import genai client = genai.Client() tools = [ {"type": "tool_search"}, { "type": "function", "name": "issue_refund", "description": "Refund an order to the original payment method.", "defer_loading": True, "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_id": {"type": "string"}, "amount": {"type": "number"}, }, "required": ["order_id", "amount"], }, }, # ... 50+ other deferred functions (leave frequent tools undeferred) ] interaction = client.interactions.create( model="gemini-4-hydrogen", input="Order A-1042 arrived damaged. Please refund 40 dollars.", tools=tools, )

Inside that single API call, the model searches for issue_refund, the API loads its schema, and the model emits the function_call. All three steps appear in interaction.steps, making it easy to inspect which tools the model considered when debugging tool names or descriptions:

"steps": [ { "type": "tool_search_call", "id": "tsc_7f2a", "arguments": {"function_names": ["issue_refund"]}, "signature": "..." }, { "type": "tool_search_result", "call_id": "tsc_7f2a", "result": [{"type": "function", "name": "issue_refund", "parameters": {...}}], "signature": "..." }, { "type": "function_call", "id": "fc_91c3", "name": "issue_refund", "arguments": {"order_id": "A-1042", "amount": 40} } ]

From here it's normal function calling: your code runs the refund and sends back a function_result.

There's no index to build or host. Gemini runs the search on the server, so the only changes to your code are the new tool and a flag on the tools you want to defer. You can keep your most-used tools loaded up front and defer the long tail.

Tool Retrieval also plays well with prefix caching. Deferred schemas stay out of the start of the prompt, and the schemas the model loads are added later in the conversation, so the cached prefix stays the same from turn to turn.

Tool Retrieval also works with remote MCP servers in the Gemini API. Set defer_loading: true on an mcp_server tool and every tool that server exposes is loaded on demand, so you can connect a large server without listing its tools one by one.

How client-side retrieval works

If you maintain your own tool registry, embedding index, or per-user permission filter, declare the tool_search with "execution": "client" and define your search parameters. Client-side retrieval adds one round trip per search, because your app runs the lookup. Tools do not need to be declared upfront, so you can also expose new tools mid-conversation when a user connects an integration:

tools = [{ "type": "tool_search", "execution": "client", "name": "search_tools", "description": "Search the internal tool registry for functions.", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["query"], }, }] # When the model emits a function_call for "search_tools", # return matching {"type": "function", ...} schemas in function_result: followup = client.interactions.create( model="gemini-4-hydrogen", previous_interaction_id=interaction.id, tools=tools, input=[{ "type": "function_result", "name": "search_tools", "call_id": step.id, "result": my_registry.search(**step.arguments), }], )

How pricing and supported models work

Tool Retrieval has no separate charge. Input and output tokens are billed at the standard rates for the model you call. Turning on tool_search adds a small, fixed block of input tokens, and each schema the model loads is billed as input for the rest of the conversation, the same as a tool declared up front. You save tokens when the schemas you never load outweigh the ones you do, which is the usual case for large libraries. Measure it against your own traffic.

Tool Retrieval works with Gemini 3.6 and later models, including all Gemini 4 models, in the Interactions API.

items.body_ko:
Tool Retrieval 기능이 이제 Gemini Interactions API에서 미리보기로 제공됩니다. 전체 도구 라이브러리를 모든 프롬프트에 보내는 대신 필요에 따라 도구 매개변수 스키마를 로드하여 입력 토큰을 줄이고 에이전트가 확장됨에 따라 도구 선택 정확도를 유지하도록 설계되었습니다.

리서치 사이언티스트, Google DeepMind

귀하의 브라우저는 오디오 요소를 지원하지 않습니다.

에이전트가 대규모 도구 라이브러리를 보다 효율적으로 관리할 수 있도록 Gemini API에 Tool Retrieval 기능을 출시합니다. 필요할 때만 매개변수 스키마를 로드하여 복잡한 작업을 위한 지연 시간과 입력 토큰 비용을 줄일 수 있습니다. 오늘 Interactions API에서 `tool_search` 도구를 추가하고 요청에서 `defer_loading`을 `true`로 설정하여 이 기능을 사용해 볼 수 있습니다.

대규모 도구 라이브러리를 관리하는 데 도움이 되는 Tool Retrieval 기능을 Gemini API에 출시합니다.

이 기능은 필요할 때만 매개변수 스키마를 로드하여 입력 토큰 수를 줄이고 지연 시간을 단축합니다.

`tool_search`를 추가하고 `defer_loading`을 `true`로 설정하여 이 기능을 활성화할 수 있습니다.

Tool Retrieval은 Gemini 3.6 이상 모델과 함께 작동하여 복잡한 에이전트 작업을 지원합니다.

개발자가 대규모 소프트웨어 도구 컬렉션을 보다 효율적으로 관리할 수 있도록 Tool Retrieval 기능을 소개합니다. 이제 에이전트는 모든 도구를 한 번에 로드하는 대신 라이브러리를 대기 상태로 유지하고 작업에 필요한 특정 세부 정보만 가져옵니다. 이렇게 하면 데이터 사용량이 줄어들고 성능이 향상되며 정확도가 향상됩니다. 최신 Gemini 모델로 이 기능을 오늘부터 사용하여 더욱 강력하고 반응성이 뛰어난 애플리케이션을 구축할 수 있습니다.

오늘 Gemini API에 Tool Retrieval 기능을 출시하며, Interactions API에서 미리보기로 사용할 수 있습니다.

에이전트가 수십 또는 수백 개의 도구에 연결할 때, 모든 요청에 대해 모든 전체 매개변수 스키마를 보내는 것은 빠르게 누적됩니다. 이는 입력 토큰 수를 부풀리고 지연 시간을 추가하며 후보 목록이 늘어남에 따라 도구 선택 정확도를 낮춥니다. Tool Retrieval을 사용하면 에이전트가 전체 도구 라이브러리를 대기 상태로 유지하고 현재 작업에 필요한 경우에만 매개변수 스키마를 로드할 수 있습니다.

Tool Retrieval을 켜려면 요청에 `tool_search` 도구를 추가하고 보류하려는 도구에 `defer_loading: true`를 설정하십시오. 모델은 모든 지연된 도구의 이름과 설명을 여전히 볼 수 있으므로 어떤 도구를 사용할 수 있는지 알 수 있지만 매개변수 스키마는 컨텍스트 외부에 유지됩니다. 모델이 도구가 필요할 때 이름으로 요청하고, API가 전체 스키마를 로드하고, 모델이 함수를 호출합니다. 이 모든 작업은 동일한 요청 내에서 이루어집니다.

```python
from google import genai
client = genai.Client()
tools = [
    {"type": "tool_search"},
    {
        "type": "function",
        "name": "issue_refund",
        "description": "Refund an order to the original payment method.",
        "defer_loading": True,
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "order_id": {"type": "string"},
                "amount": {"type": "number"},
            },
            "required": ["order_id", "amount"],
        },
    },
    # ... 50+ other deferred functions (leave frequent tools undeferred)
]
interaction = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
    input="Order A-1042 arrived damaged. Please refund 40 dollars.",
    tools=tools,
)
```

단일 API 호출 내에서 모델은 `issue_refund`를 검색하고, API는 스키마를 로드하고, 모델은 `function_call`을 내보냅니다. 이 세 단계는 `interaction.steps`에 나타나므로 도구 이름 또는 설명을 디버깅할 때 모델이 고려한 도구를 쉽게 검사할 수 있습니다.

```json
"steps": [
  {
    "type": "tool_search_call",
    "id": "tsc_7f2a",
    "arguments": {"function_names": ["issue_refund"]},
    "signature": "..."
  },
  {
    "type": "tool_search_result",
    "call_id": "tsc_7f2a",
    "result": [{"type": "function", "name": "issue_refund", "parameters": {...}}],
    "signature": "..."
  },
  {
    "type": "function_call",
    "id": "fc_91c3",
    "name": "issue_refund",
    "arguments": {"order_id": "A-1042", "amount": 40}
  }
]
```

여기서부터는 일반적인 함수 호출입니다. 코드가 환불을 실행하고 `function_result`를 다시 보냅니다.

구축하거나 호스팅할 인덱스는 없습니다. Gemini는 서버에서 검색을 실행하므로 코드 변경 사항은 새 도구와 지연하려는 도구의 플래그뿐입니다. 가장 많이 사용하는 도구는 미리 로드하고 긴 꼬리 도구는 지연시킬 수 있습니다.

Tool Retrieval은 접두사 캐싱과도 잘 작동합니다. 지연된 스키마는 프롬프트 시작 부분에 나타나지 않고, 모델이 로드하는 스키마는 대화 후반에 추가되므로 캐시된 접두사는 매 턴마다 동일하게 유지됩니다.

Tool Retrieval은 Gemini API의 원격 MCP 서버와도 작동합니다. `mcp_server` 도구에 `defer_loading: true`를 설정하면 해당 서버가 노출하는 모든 도구가 필요에 따라 로드되므로, 도구를 하나씩 나열하지 않고도 대규모 서버를 연결할 수 있습니다.

클라이언트 측 검색 작동 방식

자신만의 도구 레지스트리, 임베딩 인덱스 또는 사용자별 권한 필터를 유지하는 경우 `"execution": "client"`로 `tool_search`를 선언하고 검색 매개변수를 정의하십시오. 클라이언트 측 검색은 조회에 앱이 실행되므로 검색당 한 번의 왕복을 추가합니다. 도구를 미리 선언할 필요가 없으므로 사용자가 통합을 연결할 때 대화 중간에 새 도구를 노출할 수도 있습니다.

```python
tools =[{
  "type": "tool_search",
  "execution": "client",
  "name": "search_tools",
  "description": "Search the internal tool registry for functions.",
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}},
    "required": ["query"],
  },
}]
# When the model emits a function_call for "search_tools",
# return matching {"type": "function", ...} schemas in function_result:
followup = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
    previous_interaction_id=interaction.id,
    tools=tools,
    input=[
        {
            "type": "function_result",
            "name": "search_tools",
            "call_id": step.id,
            "result": my_registry.search(**step.arguments),
        },
    ],
)
```

가격 및 지원 모델 작동 방식

Tool Retrieval에는 별도의 요금이 없습니다. 입력 및 출력 토큰은 호출하는 모델의 표준 요율로 청구됩니다. `tool_search`를 켜면 작고 고정된 입력 토큰 블록이 추가되며, 모델이 로드하는 각 스키마는 미리 선언된 도구와 동일하게 나머지 대화에 대한 입력으로 청구됩니다. 로드하지 않는 스키마가 로드하는 스키마보다 많으면 토큰을 절약할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Launch HN: Onlook (YC W25) – An open-source developer tool for designers
items.body: Hey HN, I'm Daniel, founder of Onlook (https://github.com/onlook-dev/onlook and onlook.com).Onlook is a desktop app that puts a canvas on top of your real codebase, letting you design directly in code with the agent you already use. Over 25,000 designers and developers have supported the project, 100+ have contributed, and it's been the #1 trending repo in the world twice. We just rebuilt the entire product as an agentic design tool, and open-sourced it to the community.Here’s a demo video: (https://youtu.be/BogcYWf4siM)If you're an engineer, traditional engineering tools are largely built for convergence, whereas designers tend to explore and diverge on ideas. Onlook gives designers a familiar canvas while managing all of the dev processes that get between them and making mind-blowing designs in code. Designers can work on a multiple simultaneous worktrees that run on the real app locally, and every change lands as a PR you can review or throw away, so there aren’t mockups to rebuild.We built Onlook because we believe there needs to be a developer tool that works the way designers do.More and more, designers are expected to work in code. Designers think by seeing, drafting, arranging variations, using references, and remixing ideas. That’s why the canvas has been the signature feature of design tools because it genuinely is useful for how messy the creative process is. Most of the challenge of using engineering tools for design work is that the first half of starting a project often takes mental bandwidth in of itself (What branch am I on? What page was that last exploration on?) and the second half is constrained by configuring your coded design to present itself (prompting design tools on top of what you’ve built or making temporary navigation for that specific state).Some of you may remember our earlier Show HNs (July 2024: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=40904862, August 2024: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=41390449, May 2025: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44127653). Since then, we built a web version (too early), then a Storybook-native build (a mistake). We noticed that our desktop product from July 2024 was still getting hundreds of downloads a month despite zero promotion, so we decided to rebuild it for the new era of designers working in code.How it works…Onlook shines at exploring tons of ideas at once. Ask it to lay out every flow in your product, show every state of a component, or riff on ten versions of one screen. Your designs all show up side by side on an infinite canvas, with each frame as a real webview running your actual app with real data. Not as a mockup, but the real deal.When we built this editor, we had an epiphany that it could be a new kind of IDE for design. Design tools used to be limited to a proprietary setup or closed schema, but now you can push and pull the medium of code to get whatever result you want, so why not give agents an infinite canvas of browsers and see what they do? It turns out, the agents can figure out how to better present coded work by adjusting the urls of browser frames and arranging and resizing them on the canvas.The concept is simple, but it requires a lot of product thinking. For example, because all of the frames on the canvas share a single browser session, and Chromium only allows six connections per host per session, ten frames of the same app end up fighting over limited connections. So, we had to plan around that, and there are still tons of things we need to do to make the canvas ultra performant.Onlook is an Electron app where you can import a repo from GitHub or upload a local folder. Then, Onlook creates a git worktree, starts your dev server, and has the agent sort out missing dependencies or other requirements. You never open a terminal and everything the agent does is a normal git diff that can go to GitHub as a PR. We inject a small script into each frame that draws selection outlines and reads the page, so that way you can click an element, say "make this a card layout," and the agent knows exactly what "this" is.This time we didn't build our own agent. Onlook runs Claude Code or Codex on your own subscription, and we turn whatever the agent emits into one typed event log and draw the UI from that in our own chat interface. On top of that we give the agent a bespoke set of design-specific tools, from arranging frames on the canvas, to making suggestions, to generating multiple iterations of a selection – which is especially useful because the agent decides how to get the app into a state that you need based on your prompt.We also have our own Artifacts which are quick HTML sketches that live in the editor, but outside your repo. They’re almost like components in other design tools in that they can be carried and edited across every project but are detached from the project with no network access. As an example, you can ask the agent to turn your interface into an Artifact, and use it as a reference for another exploration, or download it as HTML and send it to a coworker as an interactive export of something you have in progress. I frequently go back to the artifacts I’ve made as visual snippets when I need new ideas or need to borrow something that’s already been built.The desktop editor is free (you can download it from our website at onlook.com) and open source under Apache-2.0, and we'll eventually offer a paid cloud product for teams.We'd love to hear which repos work and which don't, what you try to do on the canvas, and what's missing. We’re so excited for this to be a new way for designers to work in code!The Onlook team (Joel - thebrubaker and Kris - krisodd), and I will be here all day!
items.body_ko: 안녕하세요 HN, 저는 Onlook (https://github.com/onlook-dev/onlook 및 onlook.com)의 창립자 Daniel입니다.Onlook은 실제 코드베이스 위에 캔버스를 두어, 여러분이 이미 사용하는 에이전트와 함께 코드에서 직접 디자인할 수 있게 해주는 데스크톱 앱입니다. 25,000명 이상의 디자이너와 개발자들이 이 프로젝트를 지지했으며, 100명 이상이 기여했고, 두 번이나 세계에서 #1 트렌딩 리포지토리가 되었습니다. 우리는 최근 전체 제품을 에이전트 기반 디자인 도구로 재구축하고 커뮤니티에 오픈소스화했습니다.데모 영상은 여기 있습니다: (https://youtu.be/BogcYWf4siM)엔지니어라면, 전통적인 엔지니어링 도구는 주로 수렴을 위해 만들어진 반면, 디자이너는 아이디어를 탐색하고 발산하는 경향이 있습니다. Onlook은 디자이너에게 익숙한 캔버스를 제공하면서도, 코드로 놀라운 디자인을 만드는 데 방해가 되는 모든 개발 프로세스를 관리합니다. 디자이너는 로컬에서 실제 앱에서 실행되는 여러 동시 워크트리에서 작업할 수 있으며, 모든 변경 사항은 검토하거나 버릴 수 있는 PR로 착륙하므로 다시 만들 목업이 없습니다.우리는 디자이너들이 일하는 방식대로 작동하는 개발자 도구가 필요하다고 믿었기 때문에 Onlook을 만들었습니다.점점 더 많은 디자이너들이 코드에서 작업할 것으로 기대됩니다. 디자이너들은 보고, 초안을 작성하고, 변형을 배열하고, 참조를 사용하고, 아이디어를 리믹스하는 방식으로 생각합니다. 이것이 캔버스가 디자인 도구의 시그니처 기능인 이유입니다. 창의적인 과정이 얼마나 복잡한지에 실제로 유용하기 때문입니다. 디자인 작업에 엔지니어링 도구를 사용하는 데 가장 큰 어려움은 프로젝트를 시작하는 첫 번째 절반이 종종 그 자체로 정신적 대역폭을 소모하고 (어떤 브랜치에 있더라? 마지막 탐색은 어떤 페이지에 있었지?) 두 번째 절반은 코딩된 디자인을 표시하도록 구성하는 데 제약을 받는다는 것입니다 (만든 것 위에 디자인 도구를 프롬프트하거나 해당 특정 상태를 위해 임시 탐색을 만드는 것).일부 분들은 저희의 이전 Show HN을 기억하실 것입니다 (2024년 7월: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=40904862, 2024년 8월: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=41390449, 2025년 5월: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44127653). 그 이후로, 우리는 웹 버전을 만들었고 (너무 일찍), 그 다음 Storybook-native 빌드를 만들었습니다 (실수였습니다). 우리는 2024년 7월의 데스크톱 제품이 아무런 홍보 없이도 매달 수백 건의 다운로드를 기록하고 있다는 것을 알아차렸고, 그래서 코드로 작업하는 디자이너들의 새로운 시대를 위해 재구축하기로 결정했습니다.작동 방식...Onlook은 한 번에 수많은 아이디어를 탐색하는 데 탁월합니다. 제품의 모든 흐름을 배치하고, 구성 요소의 모든 상태를 표시하거나, 한 화면의 열 가지 버전을 만들어 보라고 요청할 수 있습니다. 여러분의 디자인은 모두 무한 캔버스에 나란히 표시되며, 각 프레임은 실제 데이터를 사용하는 실제 앱을 실행하는 실제 웹뷰입니다. 목업이 아니라 진짜입니다.이 에디터를 만들 때, 우리는 이것이 디자인을 위한 새로운 종류의 IDE가 될 수 있다는 깨달음을 얻었습니다. 디자인 도구는 이전에 독점적인 설정이나 폐쇄된 스키마에 제한되었지만, 이제 코드 매체를 밀고 당겨서 원하는 결과를 얻을 수 있는데, 왜 에이전트에게 무한한 브라우저 캔버스를 제공하고 그들이 무엇을 하는지 보지 않을까요? 에이전트가 브라우저 프레임의 URL을 조정하고 캔버스에 배치 및 크기를 조절하여 코딩된 작업을 더 잘 제시하는 방법을 알아낼 수 있다는 것이 밝혀졌습니다.개념은 간단하지만, 많은 제품 사고가 필요합니다. 예를 들어, 캔버스의 모든 프레임이 단일 브라우저 세션을 공유하고, Chromium은 세션당 호스트당 6개의 연결만 허용하기 때문에, 동일한 앱의 10개 프레임이 제한된 연결을 놓고 싸우게 됩니다. 그래서 우리는 이것을 염두에 두고 계획해야 했고, 캔버스를 초고성능으로 만들기 위해 아직 해야 할 일이 많습니다.Onlook은 GitHub에서 리포지토리를 가져오거나 로컬 폴더를 업로드할 수 있는 Electron 앱입니다. 그런 다음 Onlook은 git worktree를 만들고, 개발 서버를 시작하며, 에이전트가 누락된 종속성 또는 기타 요구 사항을 해결하도록 합니다. 터미널을 열 필요가 없으며 에이전트가 수행하는 모든 작업은 GitHub에 PR로 보낼 수 있는 일반적인 git diff입니다. 우리는 각 프레임에 선택 윤곽을 그리고 페이지를 읽는 작은 스크립트를 삽입하여 요소를 클릭하고 "이것을 카드 레이아웃으로 만들어"라고 말하면 에이전트가 "이것"이 무엇인지 정확히 알 수 있습니다.이번에는 우리 고유의 에이전트를 만들지 않았습니다. Onlook은 여러분의 구독을 통해 Claude Code 또는 Codex를 실행하며, 에이전트가 내보내는 모든 것을 하나의 타입 지정된 이벤트 로그로 변환하고 우리 고유의 채팅 인터페이스에서 UI를 그립니다. 그 위에 우리는 에이전트에게 캔버스에 프레임을 배열하고, 제안을 하고, 선택의 여러 반복을 생성하는 등 디자인 특정 도구 세트를 제공합니다. 이는 에이전트가 프롬프트에 따라 필요한 상태로 앱을 가져오는 방법을 결정하기 때문에 특히 유용합니다.또한 우리는 에디터에 존재하지만 리포지토리 외부에 있는 빠른 HTML 스케치인 우리 고유의 Artifacts를 가지고 있습니다. 이는 다른 디자인 도구의 구성 요소와 유사하게 모든 프로젝트에서 전달하고 편집할 수 있지만 네트워크 액세스 없이 프로젝트와 분리됩니다. 예를 들어, 에이전트에게 인터페이스를 Artifact로 변환하도록 요청하고, 다른 탐색을 위한 참조로 사용하거나, HTML로 다운로드하여 진행 중인 작업의 대화형 내보내기로 동료에게 보낼 수 있습니다. 저는 새로운 아이디어가 필요하거나 이미 만들어진 것을 빌려야 할 때 제가 만든 아티팩트를 시각적 스니펫으로 자주 다시 찾아봅니다.데스크톱 에디터는 무료이며 (onlook.com 웹사이트에서 다운로드할 수 있습니다) Apache-2.0 라이선스 하에 오픈소스이며, 궁극적으로 팀을 위한 유료 클라우드 제품을 제공할 것입니다.어떤 리포지토리가 작동하고 어떤 리포지토리가 작동하지 않는지, 캔버스에서 무엇을 시도하는지, 무엇이 부족한지 듣고 싶습니다. 디자이너들이 코드로 작업하는 새로운 방식이 되기를 매우 기대합니다!Onlook 팀 (Joel - thebrubaker 및 Kris - krisodd)과 저는 하루 종일 여기에 있을 것입니다!

items.title: Show HN: Foolscap – a writing app that reads your book and never writes for you
items.body:
People are scared of their ability to write and think atrophying, so I wondered: what if I built something that enhanced human creativity instead of destroying it by doing the thinking and writing for people? Foolscap is the result, or at least the first version of that idea that's fleshed out enough to share here.It reads as you write and picks out the structure: characters, ideas, threads, what's left hanging. You can respond to what it picks out, so there's a dialectic between the system and you as the writer. There's also an agent on the side, plugged into the same system, so you can ask about your book and fire off actions through conversation. It never writes into your work.The system can also follow theorems and proofs and string together their dependencies, but I haven't made that a focus yet. There's no Lean support, for example. If anyone's interested in that, I'd love to hear it.I want to build this by iterating with the people who use it: a tool that uses AI not to bypass the creative process, but to bring new tools to it. There's a free tier, and if you email hello@foolscap.works I'll send you a code for 50% off. This is my first product, so feedback of any kind is welcome.Thanks,
David

items.title: Show HN: Mastra Factory, the open-source software factory we use to build Mastra
items.body: Hi HN, we're Shane, Sam, and Abhi.Almost two years ago, we shared Mastra, our open-source TypeScript agent framework, on Show HN: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43103073. It got a few hundred upvotes; a couple of weeks later our downloads had doubled, and we were off to the races.Today we're sharing Mastra Factory, the open-source software factory we built to help maintain Mastra itself.At Mastra, we now average nearly 4M downloads per week, and with Factory our team now merges hundreds of PRs a week across the mastra-ai GitHub org. Last week, Factory opened and merged 238 PRs, alongside 630 merged PRs from humans.There's a lot of debate about what a software factory is. For us Factory is a configurable agentic kanban board that's @-taggable in Slack.Under the hood, it uses Mastra’s durable agents for long-running sessions, our conversational memory system, a markdown based wiki with source citations to incorporate company knowledge, signals that subscribe to PR comments wired up into sessions, and a customizable cloud sandbox with our coding harness (working on supporting Claude Code, Codex etc).When we started out, we modeled Factory around our existing workflow-oriented process (triage, plan, build, review, shipped). Three months later, we find ourselves mostly driving it through Slack vs a web UI.We’ve seen more senior engineers kick off sessions in parallel (“triage the 20 oldest issues and let’s evaluate…”). We’re using bug and vuln scanners now, and we’ve closed our repo to outside contributors, asking folks to write detailed issue repros instead.You can get started with `npm create factory`.It’s fully open-source, so you can run it entirely on your infra (we also offer a hosted version). Comment here, we would love to know what you think!https://factory.mastra.aihttps://github.com/mastra-ai/template-factory

items.title: Jailbreak Detection on Large Language Models via Contrastive Prototype Structures
items.body: Jailbreak attempts and harmful prompts remain a challenge for the safe deployment of large language models. We study whether contrastively learned representations can support safety detection without training an additional downstream classifier. We propose Jailbreak Detection with Prototype Inference (JDPI), which uses binary safety labels to construct harmful and benign prototypes and makes predictions from relative prototype distances. JDPI uses only binary safety labels for encoder adaptation, prototype construction, and validation. In our setup, it uses fewer labeled examples than the classifier baseline (Method A) by avoiding the separate split used to train the downstream classifier. Across four benchmarks covering different input formats, contrastive fine-tuning improves JDPI's detection accuracy by 9.1-18.0 percentage points. Using the same encoder, JDPI achieves slightly higher ROC-AUC on one benchmark and stays within 0.017 of the baseline across all four. With dataset-specific adaptation, JDPI exceeds the released Llama Guard 3-8B baseline by 0.173-0.310 in ROC-AUC across the four benchmarks. In multi-turn replay on TomGibbs, JDPI uses accumulated user history as the conversation unfolds, achieving higher conversation-level accuracy than when it uses the current turn alone. Across 12 directed transfers, JDPI outperforms the classifier by an average of 1.59 percentage points in accuracy, demonstrating stronger cross-dataset robustness.

items.title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
items.body: When a capable model and a human reviewer cooperate on the same decision, which human still adds value? We argue this is a question about a single cognitive trait, metacognitive calibration: the alignment between a reviewer's behavioral confidence and the actual correctness of their judgments. We develop a trait theory of reviewer value to make it precise. The theory makes five claims: value is governed by calibration rather than by activity, speed, agreement, or tenure; calibration leaves observable traces in behavioral telemetry; those traces are non-diagnostic on their own, because the fast, low-revision signature of a calibrated expert is indistinguishable from that of a confident novice until it is gated by outcomes; human calibration and a model's self-knowledge are the same construct, so the joint system should defer to whichever agent is better calibrated on each item; and individual calibration is causally identifiable only above the level of the single judgment. We ground each claim in a six-month production window of an AI-assisted accounting system (541621 reviewer events, 483 reviewers), and find that a purely behavioral expertise profile inverts the ground truth, scoring an overconfident cohort (5.2 percent correction survival) higher than genuine experts (99.2 percent); that reviewer quality is flat across tenure, so the trait is not learned on the job; and that the same calibration logic that separates good from bad reviewers, applied to the model, concentrates 92.5 percent of human effort on genuine errors. We close with the boundary the theory must respect: under majority-vote aggregation, individual causal value is unidentifiable.

items.title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
items.body: AI systems are built across many organizations that contribute models, data, compute, capital, talent, and other assets. While the layers of the AI stack are relatively well understood, the relationships between actors and components across layers remains sparsely documented. In this work, we focus on the organizations that make up the AI supply chain: the complex network of actors that contribute to the development and deployment of AI. We motivate the examination of the organizational AI supply chain---highlighting concerns about concentration, power, chokepoints, cascading failures, fragmented accountability, and risk---then describe our pipeline for mapping the AI supply chain. Our pipeline yields our main contribution: a multilayered, large-scale dataset of actors and relationships in the AI ecosystem, annotated with dates, descriptions, types, tags, and more. This work takes a step toward systematically mapping and measuring the AI supply chain and its properties, cataloging how models, data, chips, infrastructure, capital, and even talent flow between organizations. This data enable critical examinations of industry relationships and yield insights into the political economy of AI development and concentration. We provide several illustrative analyses, including studying the most central actors, analyzing network concentration, and identifying communities and chokepoints. While our dataset is fairly comprehensive, it is also necessarily incomplete: public documents omit private deals, and coverage is shaped by search design. Together, the approach, data, and findings aim to serve as a resource for studying the AI ecosystem. The dataset is publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/sarahcen/ai-supply-chain and can be explored interactively at https://aisupplychains.org/.

items.title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
items.body: Real-world harness engineering is driven by explicit and implicit user requirements, which guide development and validation. However, existing harness evolution methods often overlook implicit requirements and interaction needs, while using a single evolution agent to modify the harness and benchmark scores to select changes. This process often produces narrow patches and leads to benchmark-specific local optima. We introduce Agentic Harness Engineering Beta (AHE-Beta), a requirement-centered loop that brings real-world engineering practices into harness evolution. The loop consists of three steps: (1) User-driven evaluation lets simulated users raise their requirements as issues while they work with the harness over multiple turns. (2) Team-based modification implements those requirements as generalizable changes rather than task-specific patches. (3) Requirement-driven selection merges a change only when it resolves a verified requirement and passes review. Empirically, on held-out tasks, AHE-Beta raises pass@1 from 21.9% to 33.3% while using 40.8% fewer tokens than Base Harness, and achieves higher pass@1 than Claude Code, Meta-Harness, and AHE. In a blind human A/B test, real users prefer AHE-Beta in 31 of 48 valid pairs and rate it higher on all five dimensions, matching the directional preference of the user simulator. The human A/B results show that AHE-Beta achieves its goal of aligning harness evolution with real-world user requirements. Without further evolution, the gains transfer to GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with pass@1 improvements of 15.8% and 5.3% over Base Harness. Together, these results show that requirement-centered harness evolution is a more general method for improving agent capabilities.

items.title: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation
items.body: We study two-layer neural networks trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on a multi-index teacher model, focusing on how first-layer parameters orthogonal to the teacher subspace affect generalization. We decompose the first-layer weights into a signal component aligned with the teacher and an orthogonal complement, and analyze their joint SGD dynamics together with the second layer in the proportional limit. We show that although SGD updates to the complement are initially isotropic, the training dynamics induce teacher-dependent spectral spikes in the complement Gram matrix. This emergent anisotropy provides a concrete mechanism by which representation variance is amplified, and generalization degrades. To isolate this effect, we introduce Decomposed Dynamics, an analytically tractable surrogate whose asymptotic test-error dynamics coincide with those of SGD. In simulations with a ReLU student, freezing the directions of the orthogonal complement improves generalization relative to training them. Finally, we show that the signal component rapidly aligns with the second-layer weights, revealing strong cross-layer coupling even in this shallow setting. Together, our results provide a dynamical explanation for how feature learning outside the teacher subspace harms generalization.

items.title: Equivariant Modeling with Polynomial Features via Minimal Homogeneous Generators
items.body: We present a general framework for modeling and learning equivariant functions between finite dimensional semisimple real group representations, unifying constructions developed across many application areas. Our model is a linear combination of equivariant polynomial features whose coefficients are arbitrary learnable functions of invariant polynomial features. We take as features minimal homogeneous generators for the invariant algebra and the covariant module over the invariant algebra, up to prescribed degrees. We provide a Python package that automatically computes these features and fits the resulting models to training data. The algorithm for feature computation requires explicit isotypic decompositions of the input and output representations, along with explicit Clebsch-Gordan decompositions of the tensor product of irreducible representations, and achieves speedups over alternative methods in computational algebra. Numerical experiments in scientific modeling demonstrate the full learning pipeline and yield accurate predictors with few trainable parameters, using the model both for end-to-end prediction and within layers of larger architectures.
items.title_ko: 최소 동차 생성자를 통한 다항식 특징을 이용한 등변량 모델링
items.summary_ko: 유한 차원 반단순 실수 군 표현 사이의 등변량 함수 모델링 및 학습을 위한 일반적인 프레임워크를 제시합니다. 이 모델은 등변량 다항식 특징의 선형 조합으로 구성되며, 계수는 불변 다항식 특징의 임의의 학습 가능한 함수입니다.
items.why_ko: 다양한 응용 분야에서 개발된 구조를 통합하는 등변량 모델링에 대한 새로운 접근 방식을 제시하여, 모델의 일반화 및 효율성을 향상시키는 데 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents
items.body: User simulators offer a scalable way to evaluate interactive agents, but how to assess their quality remains underexplored. In particular, it is unclear whether existing user simulator evaluation frameworks reliably detect meaningful failures in simulated user behavior. This uncertainty makes it difficult to interpret simulator evaluation. To understand what a high benchmark score tells us about simulator quality, we (meta-)evaluate the metrics themselves. To instantiate this meta-evaluation, we deliberately perturb simulated replays to induce failures such as altered goals, omitted constraints, premature stopping, and acceptance of broken work, then test whether the metrics penalize these failures. Evaluation methods from three prior studies detect only 5-6 of the 10 perturbations; their combined scores even favor populations instructed to accept broken work over unmodified controls. Motivated by these gaps, we propose a new evaluation suite that combines utility of user simulators for evaluating agents and two measures of fidelity to real users: population-level fidelity assesses collective interaction patterns, while trace-level fidelity assesses the preservation of individual users' goals, constraints, and persona. Under the same detection criterion, our evaluation suite detects all 10 perturbations. Evaluating six user simulators on 351 real multi-turn sessions in which 348 distinct users across 23 languages and agents work together to create and refine artifacts such as full-stack web apps, games, design assets, and automated workflows, we find that population-level measures can miss when a simulated user pursues the wrong goal, ignores a constraint, or behaves out of character, highlighting the need to assess fidelity at comprehensive granularities.
items.title_ko: 인터랙티브 에이전트를 위한 사용자 시뮬레이터 평가에 대하여
items.summary_ko: 인터랙티브 에이전트 평가를 위한 확장 가능한 방법으로 사용자 시뮬레이터가 사용되지만, 그 품질을 평가하는 방법은 충분히 탐구되지 않았습니다. 이 연구는 사용자 시뮬레이터 평가 프레임워크가 시뮬레이션된 사용자 행동의 중요한 실패를 신뢰할 수 있게 감지하는지에 대한 불확실성을 해소하고자 합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트 개발에서 사용자 시뮬레이터의 중요성이 커지고 있으므로, 시뮬레이터의 신뢰성을 평가하는 방법을 이해하는 것은 에이전트의 효과적인 테스트 및 개선에 필수적입니다.

items.title: Cap-and-Track: Optimizing LLM Inference Request Dispatch Across Shifting Capacity
items.body: A fixed dispatch rate for LLM inference becomes stale as serving fleets resize and request sizes change. Generative output length is unknown at admission, and shared provider pools can lose capacity. We present Cap-and-Track, a design for asynchronous inference across provider capacity and internal GPUs. Meta's traffic shaper implements Cap-and-Track for post and live-video understanding. Refusals signal the backend's current admission ceiling. Durable priority queues hold excess work outside execution, including refused requests for retry. Cap is a fail-fast admission check at the saturated resource that refuses work before a long wait. Using only those refusals, the Track dispatcher probes upward and backs off. It follows the ceiling without output-length prediction or a fleet-level rate to retune. In a concurrent same-traffic production A/B, the shaper ran per-replica Cap plus Track. It served a classifier on 43% fewer H100s than its queued, fixed-rate precursor, though lower-priority work waited longer at backfill peaks. In steady-capacity real-engine replay, Track ran within 1% of the goodput of a fixed rate tuned above measured capacity, with about a quarter of that rate's refusal share. The shaper carries more than 300 million online requests and hundreds of terabytes of media a day. During a backfill, it handled 1.1 billion requests in its busiest 24 hours. Lessons include keeping queues inside inference engines just long enough to fill batches, steering dispatch by capacity refusals alone, keeping dispatch stateful, and sizing fleets by how long low-priority work can wait.
items.title_ko: Cap-and-Track: 변화하는 용량에 따른 LLM 추론 요청 디스패치 최적화
items.summary_ko: LLM 추론을 위한 고정된 디스패치 속도는 서빙 플릿 규모나 요청 크기가 변함에 따라 비효율적이 됩니다. Cap-and-Track은 메타의 트래픽 셰이퍼에 구현된 비동기 추론 디자인으로, 백엔드의 현재 수용 상한을 거부 신호로 사용하고, 영구 우선순위 큐를 통해 초과 작업을 처리합니다.
items.why_ko: 대규모 LLM 서비스를 운영할 때 동적으로 변하는 자원과 요청에 효율적으로 대응하는 것은 핵심적인 엔지니어링 과제이며, Cap-and-Track은 실용적인 해결책을 제시합니다.

items.title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game
items.body: Large Language Models (LLMs) now perform strongly on Alan Turing's 1950 Imitation Game, so we propose a harder challenge, the Personal Imitation Game, which asks whether a machine can replicate a specific individual in conversation rather than a generic human. Testing with 30 participants, we establish a human baseline and report the identity signals interrogators rely on: stylometric features, personality traits, and biographical facts. To demonstrate the framework, we design an LLM-based system that plays the game for one of the paper's authors, drawing on an autoethnographic dataset spanning ten years of personal digital communication. In a 20-person deception study, interrogators choose our system over the author's own friends in 7 of 10 rounds, and the author over our system in 13 of 20; neither rate is distinguishable from chance at this sample size. We consider design improvements, applications of personal AI agents, and implications for identity and privacy.
items.title_ko: 당신은 누구인가? 개인 모방 게임 (Personal Imitation Game)
items.summary_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)이 튜링 테스트에서 강력한 성능을 보여줌에 따라, 특정 개인을 대화에서 복제할 수 있는지 묻는 더 어려운 도전 과제인 '개인 모방 게임'이 제안되었습니다. 30명의 참가자를 대상으로 실험하여 심문관이 의존하는 정체성 신호를 파악했습니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 인간 모방 능력을 심층적으로 이해하는 것은 AI의 사회적 영향과 윤리적 측면을 탐구하는 데 중요하며, 더욱 정교한 대화형 AI 개발에 영감을 줍니다.

items.title: Ground, Iterate, Trace: Decomposing AI Research Ideation
items.body: Large language models have been widely used to generate plausible research ideas, yet it remains unclear what makes automated ideation effective and how generated novel proposals arise from prior scientific work. We introduce the Creative AI Researcher (CAR), an agentic framework combining literature grounding, iterative development and explicit conceptual operators. CAR constructs a semantic knowledge graph from retrieved literature and equips an ideation agent with graph-retrieval tools and four operators: bisociation, analogy, exploration and elaboration. Each operator call is checked against structural acceptance conditions and recorded, producing a trace of intermediate transformations and declared literature sources. We evaluate CAR with two language-model backbones across 40 LiveIdeaBench research topics and two execution benchmarks. CAR achieves significantly higher methodological novelty (MN) than single-shot prompting and The AI Scientist. Its methodological novelty does not differ significantly from the Research Ideation Agent, while its feasibility scores are higher on both backbones. With a shared experiment executor, CAR achieves the highest pairwise win rate among the evaluated AI methods on FML-bench-Lite and BioXArena. In a ten-condition ablation study, MN point estimates favor CAR over one-step proposal on both backbones, but no MN contrast survives correction for multiple comparisons. The results do not establish a consistent quality benefit from explicit operators beyond free-form iteration. CAR makes the sequence of operations and declared literature sources inspectable, separating judged idea quality from procedural traceability.
items.title_ko: Ground, Iterate, Trace: AI 연구 아이디어 발상 분해
items.summary_ko: Creative AI Researcher (CAR)은 문헌 기반 연구, 반복적인 개발, 명시적 개념 연산자를 결합한 에이전트 프레임워크입니다. CAR은 검색된 문헌에서 의미론적 지식 그래프를 구축하고, 그래프 검색 도구와 개념 연산자를 아이디어 발상 에이전트에 제공하여 자동화된 아이디어 발상의 효과성과 과학적 선행 연구로부터 새로운 제안이 어떻게 발생하는지 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: AI를 활용하여 연구 아이디어를 생성하는 과정에 대한 이해를 높이고, 연구자들이 보다 효율적으로 새로운 아이디어를 발상할 수 있는 도구를 개발하는 데 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Monoculture Robust Learning
items.body: We introduce a notion of monoculture robustness in Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning, as a way to mitigate the problem of algorithmic monoculture (Kleinberg and Raghavan, 2021): the tendency of models sharing the same components (e.g., training data) to fail on the same inputs. Specifically, we ask whether a learner with access to a single dataset can output $k$ individually accurate hypotheses whose joint failure probability is comparable to training on $k$ independent datasets. We say that such a learning procedure achieves monoculture robustness, and we quantify this by bounding the conjunctive error that all $k$ hypotheses misclassify points in an individual sense. We design methods for achieving this type of guarantee by drawing a surprising connection between replicability (Impagliazzo et al., 2022) and monoculture robustness. Specifically, we show that if the base learner is $ρ$-replicable, then running it independently $k$ times on the same sample yields individual monoculture error that shrinks exponentially with $k$, controlled by the single-run error of the base learner at the point and $ρ$. We complement these positive results with a lower bound: for individual monoculture robustness, we prove a worst-case lower bound showing that, for learners, driving the individual conjunctive error down to $γ$ can require a sample-size multiplier of $t = Ω(\log(1/γ))$.
items.title_ko: 단일 문화 강건 학습: 알고리즘 단일 문화 문제 완화
items.summary_ko: 알고리즘 단일 문화(algorithmic monoculture) 문제를 완화하기 위한 '단일 문화 강건 학습(monoculture robustness)' 개념을 PAC(Probably Approximately Correct) 학습에 도입했습니다. 이 연구는 단일 데이터셋으로 학습된 k개의 가설이 k개의 독립적인 데이터셋으로 학습된 경우와 유사한 공동 실패 확률을 갖는지 질문합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 모델이 동일한 구성 요소를 공유할 때 발생하는 집단 오류를 줄이는 것은 AI 시스템의 신뢰성과 다양성을 높이는 데 중요한 과제입니다.

items.title: Local AI Agents in Power Electronics Simulation: Deployment, Measurements and Costs
items.body: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging in power electronics, where it drives the simulation loop that engineers used to close largely by hand. In this loop, a converter design, or a study of the network it connects to, is built, run, measured and revised until it satisfies its specification. Such an agent can be served from a cloud API or from an inference device on the premises. For organizations whose designs, customer data or export-controlled material cannot leave the site, and whose simulators are licensed there, local deployment is the natural choice. In such a deployment, the agent becomes an electrical load on the organization's own equipment, i.e., every run consumes power and energy on a local device, generates tokens and takes time. However, existing work focuses mainly on what the agent can achieve with cloud-hosted models. What a local deployment costs in power, energy, tokens and time on real simulation tasks, and what its choices trade against one another, has received little quantitative investigation under comparable conditions. To address this gap, a systematic evaluation framework is presented in this paper. It applies locally served models to agentic power electronics tasks, from the converter level to the system level, and measures their power, energy, token and time costs. Based on these measurements, the capability boundary of a local agent on such tasks and the cost per solved task are characterized. The results are expected to provide practical insight for the use of agentic AI in power electronics and the power systems it serves.
items.title_ko: 전력 전자 시뮬레이션의 로컬 AI 에이전트: 배포, 측정 및 비용
items.summary_ko: 전력 전자 시뮬레이션에서 AI 에이전트가 등장하여 엔지니어들이 수동으로 처리하던 시뮬레이션 루프를 주도합니다. 이 연구는 로컬 AI 에이전트의 배포, 측정 및 비용에 대해 논의하며, 특히 온프레미스 환경에서의 중요성을 강조합니다.
items.why_ko: 엣지 AI 에이전트의 실제 산업 적용 가능성을 보여주며, 데이터 보안 및 처리 속도 면에서 중요한 이점을 제공하여 개발자들이 고려할 만한 새로운 아키텍처를 제시합니다.

items.title: Auditing black-box clinical prediction models with a large language model through queries alone: a blinded test with planted flaws
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) are used to explain clinical prediction models, on the promise that they can say what a model computes, find its faults and even reveal new knowledge in it. We tested the three promises where the answers could be checked. From the International Stroke Trial we trained four kinds of model (logistic regression, explainable boosting machine, gradient-boosted trees, neural network) for two outcomes on patients randomised earlier, planted one flaw in each of 24 copies (an under-predicted subgroup, a reversed risk factor or an implausible step) and mixed them with the 8 clean models. GPT-6 Astra audited each model three times, blind, through a tool that only returned the model's predictions; the judging rules were committed before any run and applied by program. Its surrogate models, with a median of 128 terms, reproduced the audited models' log-odds with a mean $R^2$ of 0.976 (0.959 for an additive surrogate of 42 terms fitted by an analyst). It found the planted flaw in 69 of 72 runs (96%; 95% CI 80% to 99%); a script written for the purpose found all 24. It also reported many more problems: 60% of 1,089 checkable reports failed the pre-specified check against the model's average behaviour; post hoc, most of these were real but small steps, and 15% of the checkable reports were not found in the model. Of 601 unexpected relationships it read out of the clean models, 11% held in patients randomised later (random pairs 6%; a regression scan's shorter list of its strongest candidates, 28%); after a check on the training data, 33% against 30%. With query access alone, an LLM can describe a black-box model faithfully and find nearly every planted flaw, as a purpose-written script also did; its reports of problems must be checked on the model and its discoveries on data.
items.title_ko: 쿼리만으로 블랙박스 임상 예측 모델 감사: 결함을 심은 맹검 테스트
items.summary_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)을 사용하여 블랙박스 임상 예측 모델을 감사하는 능력을 테스트했습니다. 국제 뇌졸중 시험 데이터를 기반으로 4가지 모델에 결함을 심어 LLM이 모델의 계산 방식과 결함을 찾아낼 수 있는지 평가했습니다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 복잡한 블랙박스 모델의 이해와 감사에 활용될 가능성을 보여주며, AI의 신뢰성과 투명성을 높이는 데 중요한 시사점을 제공합니다.

items.title: Learning to Interact in Multi-Agent Self-Play for Controllable Autonomous Driving Scenario Generation
items.body: Large-scale, multi-agent self-play trains robust driving policies effectively in simulation, but controlling these models to generate specific, safety-critical edge cases remains a key challenge. Existing goal-conditioned self-play frameworks rely primarily on static map-location goals and fail to reliably produce complex agent interactions such as aggressive tailgating or adversarial cut-offs. These agent interactions are necessary for rigorous autonomous vehicle (AV) testing. To address this, we present an extended multi-agent self-play framework that introduces agent-relative dynamic goals. By conditioning policies on this extended goal representation, our framework enables targeted, controllable scenario synthesis. We demonstrate that our approach successfully generates interactive driving behaviors that static-goal baselines cannot simulate, providing a flexible tool for long-tail scenario generation in AV testing.
items.title_ko: 자율주행 시나리오 생성을 위한 다중 에이전트 자가 학습 상호작용 학습
items.summary_ko: 대규모 다중 에이전트 자가 학습은 시뮬레이션에서 강력한 주행 정책을 효과적으로 훈련시키지만, 안전에 중요한 특정 엣지 케이스를 생성하도록 제어하는 것이 어렵습니다. 이 연구는 복잡한 에이전트 상호작용을 안정적으로 생성하기 위한 새로운 접근 방식을 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: 자율주행의 안전성 검증을 위한 실제와 같은 시나리오 생성은 핵심 기술이며, AI 에이전트의 상호작용 학습은 더욱 현실적인 테스트 환경을 구축하는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: TangentPDE: Learning Local Operator Responses with Sparse Finite-Difference Supervision
items.body: Neural PDE operators are often optimized through state reconstruction, which largely constrains operator values at observed inputs but does not fully characterize their sensitivity to local perturbations. A more faithful approximation of operator behavior requires not only accurate state predictions, but also correct variations along local perturbation directions. We present TangentPDE, which uses finite differences to approximate directional derivatives and constructs task-relevant finite-step responses from the state outputs of a reference solver at sparse paired inputs. Its objective jointly constrains state fidelity, response-direction alignment, and response-magnitude calibration, thereby learning both operator values and their local variations. Because the response labels are constructed solely from state outputs at paired inputs, the method requires neither explicit derivative labels, linearized or adjoint PDE solves, nor full Jacobians, and remains applicable to nonlinear solvers without derivative interfaces. Building on this, we additionally propose a selectively executed adaptation mechanism to strengthen local operator representations under finite-difference supervision. Budget-matched and correspondence-perturbed controls isolate the effect of relational supervision from improvements attributable to additional state observations or increased data volume. Designed as a plug-and-play training framework, TangentPDE integrates with diverse neural-operator backbones. Across four PDE systems and 20 task-backbone settings, TangentPDE lowers the three-seed mean state error in 18 settings and the corresponding Rollout@20 error in 18, while intrinsic finite-step response gains are strongest on DiffReact and remain task- and backbone-dependent elsewhere.
items.title_ko: TangentPDE: 희소 유한 차분 감독을 통한 로컬 연산자 반응 학습
items.summary_ko: 신경 미분방정식(PDE) 연산자는 종종 상태 재구성을 통해 최적화되지만, 이는 관찰된 입력에서 연산자 값을 크게 제약하지만 로컬 섭동에 대한 민감도를 완전히 특성화하지 못합니다. TangentPDE는 유한 차분을 사용하여 방향 미분을 근사하고 작업 관련 유한 단계 목적 함수를 구성합니다.
items.why_ko: PDE 모델링은 과학 및 공학 분야에서 중요하며, TangentPDE는 연산자 동작을 더 정확하게 근사하여 모델의 예측 정확도와 민감도를 향상시키는 데 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
items.body: Rules govern how player actions change interactive worlds. Different rules create distinct gameplay experiences within similar scenes and action spaces. For customizable gameplay, generative world models must follow user-defined rules beyond real-world behaviors. However, realizing user-defined rules presents two challenges: Rule-State Persistence and Rule-to-Visual Realization. The former requires preserving rule definitions, dependencies, and world states across saving and loading, so that restored worlds follow the established rules. The latter requires accurately realizing rule-induced changes on designated objects and attributes, particularly when affected objects are unseen. In this paper, we propose WorldRuler, which organizes rule definitions, dependencies, and object states in an executable 3D rule graph and connects rule execution, video generation, and perceptual feedback in a closed loop. The graph supports joint saving and restoration of rules and world states, while dynamic object binding grounds rule-specified entities in visual instances and uses stored states to constrain generation from their first appearance. We further introduce object attribute state replacement and counterfactual reconstruction training, enabling accurate attribute control and compatible appearance and motion changes while limiting interference with unrelated content. We develop an automated data collection and annotation pipeline using GTA-V and Habitat to construct RuleVerse, a dataset of rule-driven interactions with detailed state and event annotations, including cases where rules take effect before affected objects become visible. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of WorldRuler in preserving rule-state consistency across saving and loading and accurately realizing rule outcomes on designated objects and attributes.
items.title_ko: WorldRuler: 구성 가능한 규칙 하의 인터랙티브 세계 모델링
items.summary_ko: WorldRuler는 사용자 정의 규칙에 따라 플레이어의 행동이 인터랙티브 세계를 어떻게 변화시키는지 모델링하는 프레임워크입니다. 이는 규칙-상태 지속성 및 규칙-시각화 구현의 두 가지 과제를 해결하여 맞춤형 게임 플레이를 가능하게 합니다.

items.title: Choosing What to Observe: Budget-Paired Counterfactual Audits for Credible Evaluation of Visual Agents
items.body: Visual agents that read dense documents must ration a finite observation budget across candidate regions, yet answer accuracy conflates where an agent looks, how it adapts to the reads that remain, and how it an?swers once observation stops. items.title: Can Programs Replace LLM Judges? Executable Program Judges for Scalable and Efficient Relevance Labeling
items.body: Large language model (LLM) judges have become a common way to create large-scale relevance judgments for retrieval evaluation. However, each judgment requires a potentially expensive call to a frontier model, and the judgments are hard to interpret and may not be reproducible. In this paper, we ask whether an LLM can write a readable program for each topic that replaces its per-document judgments. To address these issues, we propose ExecJudges, a method for generating fast, inspectable and scalable judges for automatic relevance labeling. Specifically, ExecJudges uses a frontier LLM to turn assessment guidelines into executable programs, which rely only on lexical matching, standard NLP libraries like parsers, and pool statistics. An ExecJudges-L variant also uses examples of human labels if available. We evaluate ExecJudges on seven TREC collections by comparing the produced labels with trained NIST assessors, frontier LLM judges, and recently proposed per-topic classifiers. Our results show that ExecJudges agrees with NIST assessors at the level of the Claude Sonnet 5.5 LLM judges on TREC DL 2019-2021. With a small number of human labels per topic, the ExecJudges-L variant agrees with NIST more than per-topic classifiers with the same labels on all seven collections, and either exceeds the agreement of LLM judges provided the same labels or is within about 0.05 of it in Krippendorff's alpha. The labels rank the official TREC DL runs with Kendall's tau of 0.87 to 0.94, and writing the programs incurs a one-time cost of $0.17 to $0.49 per topic, with no additional costs for grading. Our results suggest that ExecJudges offers a reproducible, inspectable, efficient and cost-effective alternative to LLM judges for labeling deep result pools for system evaluation or ranking improvements.

items.title: Atomic MathReasoner: Instance-Level Composition of Atomic Reasoning Skills for Mathematical LLMs
items.body: Most existing approaches enhance mathematical reasoning in large language models (LLMs) as a monolithic capability, despite the fact that different mathematical problems require different reasoning skills. Recent work has explored a more fine-grained perspective by decomposing mathematical reasoning into atomic skills and developing specialized modules for individual capabilities. However, how to effectively utilize these atomic abilities remains underexplored. To address this challenge, we propose Atomic MathReasoner (AMR), an instance-level framework for composing atomic reasoning skills. AMR first trains a library of capability-specific LoRA experts and performs gradient-free optimization over held-out validation subsets to discover a diverse set of low-loss composition prototypes. It evaluates the preference of each prototype using the token-level negative log-likelihood of reference solutions, filters ambiguous assignments through a confidence margin, and distills the resulting pseudo-labels into a lightweight router. During inference, the router selects an appropriate composition prototype for each problem, enabling problem-specific utilization of atomic skills without costly online optimization. Experiments on the AtomicMath benchmark across general and mathematics-specialized LLMs demonstrate consistent improvements. On Qwen2.5-Math-Instruct-7B, AMR increases average field accuracy from 64.4% to 68.1% at Level 1 and from 59.3% to 63.7% at Level 2, while improving average logical reasoning performance from 39.4% to 46.8%. These results demonstrate that effectively composing specialized atomic skills provides a promising approach to strengthening mathematical reasoning in LLMs.
items.title_ko: Atomic MathReasoner: 수학 LLM을 위한 원자적 추론 기술의 인스턴스 수준 구성
items.summary_ko: 대부분의 접근 방식이 LLM의 수학적 추론 능력을 통합적인 능력으로 강화하는 반면, Atomic MathReasoner는 수학적 추론을 원자적 기술로 분해하고, 이러한 원자적 능력을 효과적으로 활용하는 인스턴스 수준 구성 방법을 제안합니다.

items.title: Vibe-Trading: Towards Agent-Native Trading
items.body: Existing AI agents can retrieve information, call tools, run experiments, and produce multi-step outputs. Yet most are built around relatively static workflows and struggle to preserve reliable state as the environment changes. Financial trading makes this limitation especially consequential: prices, news, market conditions, portfolio positions, and available capital evolve continuously. A result is useful only when it remains tied to the correct time, data snapshot, and execution context. We present Vibe-Trading, a comprehensive agent-native trading framework and all-in-one workspace for building, evaluating, and evolving agents for financial trading. It unifies market research, financial data, strategy generation, backtesting, portfolio analysis, paper trading, multi-agent collaboration, and optional broker execution. Its central contribution is an architecture that keeps results, evidence, research history, and trading authority connected throughout the research-to-action process. Each result retains its source, temporal scope, configuration, and producing run. Shared evidence grounding enables verification, versioned research records support reproducible continuation, and an explicit authority gate separates strategy research from live execution. Together, these designs provide a practical foundation for trading agents whose results can be traced, reproduced, and acted on only under explicit authority.
items.title_ko: Vibe-Trading: 에이전트 네이티브 트레이딩을 향하여
items.summary_ko: 기존 AI 에이전트는 정보 검색, 도구 호출, 실험 실행 및 다단계 출력 생성이 가능하지만, 환경이 변할 때 신뢰할 수 있는 상태를 유지하는 데 어려움을 겪습니다. Vibe-Trading은 이러한 한계가 금융 트레이딩에서 특히 중요하다는 점을 지적하며 에이전트 네이티브 트레이딩의 필요성을 강조합니다.
items.why_ko: 빠르게 변화하는 금융 시장에서 AI 에이전트가 실시간으로 정보를 처리하고 의사결정을 내리는 것은 중요한 기술적 도전이며, 이 연구는 에이전트 기반 트레이딩 시스템 개발에 대한 통찰을 제공합니다.

items.title: General progress substitutes for specific training data in language models
items.body: Language models acquire their capabilities from training data, and developers withhold data during training to keep models from learning capabilities that could be misused. How long this delays a capability, and how much data is needed to acquire it later, is unknown. Here we show that the general progress a model makes on the rest of its training data substitutes for the data that was withheld. We withheld the training signal for individual skills in models of chess, Othello, molecular strings, bracket languages and web text. The delay of a withheld skill in larger models was predicted from smaller ones. A chess model never explicitly trained to respond to check ranked the legal responses almost as well as a model that was. When models were then trained on the withheld data, they acquired the skill with a small fraction of the data needed from initialization, and this fraction decreased as the models progressed. A control rule of equal difficulty was learned much more slowly. A programming language withheld from the training text of a 7-billion-parameter model was regained in the same way. Data filtering therefore delays a capability, and the data required to regain it decreases as models improve.

items.title: Measuring and Improving Transfer of Neural Surrogates for Vehicle Aerodynamics
items.body: Neural surrogates for external vehicle aerodynamics are fast alternatives to physics-based computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. Their foundational limitation is a lack of zero-shot generalization across vehicle classes, which results in an expensive, custom training campaign for each new vehicle design. Similar to pretrained models in other fields, a pretrained surrogate should adapt to a new vehicle class using only a few simulations and stay accurate on its pretraining domain. No prior study has systematically tested this transfer behavior. We conduct a large-scale, controlled benchmarking study on five DrivAerML-pretrained surrogates across four independent target datasets. These datasets differ from the source in geometry, CFD solver, turbulence model, and flow conditions. We find that fine-tuning these surrogates outperforms training from scratch in fewer than half of the comparisons and lowers the accuracy of the surrogate on its source dataset. We introduce GeoReplay, a geometry- and gradient-aligned source replay that keeps source simulations resembling the target in training and applies their updates only when they agree with the target gradient. A risk bound separates geometric coverage from differences in the simulated physics, and we prove that every sufficiently small GeoReplay step decreases the target training objective. GeoReplay lowers the source error of fine-tuning in 77 of 80 settings and matches its target accuracy.

items.title: Does the Action Matter? Probing Action-Conditioned Semantic Forecasting as a World Model for Autonomous Driving
items.body: World models are increasingly used in autonomous driving to predict how a scene evolves under the ego vehicle's actions, supporting counterfactual reasoning and model-based planning. However, existing evaluations focus on prediction fidelity and planning performance, and rarely verify that the predictions depend on the conditioning action. In this paper, we study action dependence in action-conditioned semantic forecasting, which predicts future semantic segmentation from past segmentations and the ego action. We compare a forecaster with feature-wise and input-level action conditioning against an identical model without action input, and measure action dependence with test-time action interventions scored by standard segmentation metrics. The evaluation is validated in a synthetic environment with known action-dependent dynamics and applied to Cityscapes and BDD100K, both within each dataset and across the two vehicle platforms. Experiments show that the executed action improves mid-term mIoU by at most 2.5 points on Cityscapes and 0.6 points on BDD100K, whereas a wrong action reduces it by up to 23.2 and 7.0 points, below the model without action input. On real data, feature-wise conditioning depends 1.6 times more on the action than input-level conditioning at similar accuracy, whereas both depend on it equally in the synthetic environment, where the history does not determine the action. These results show that an accuracy gain indicates that a driving world model uses its action, but not how strongly its forecasts depend on it. Code is available at https://github.com/binayksingh/does-action-matter.
items.title_ko: 행동이 중요한가? 자율주행을 위한 월드 모델로서 행동 조건부 의미론적 예측 조사
items.summary_ko: 월드 모델은 자율주행에서 차량의 행동에 따라 장면이 어떻게 변화하는지 예측하는 데 사용됩니다. 이 연구는 기존 평가가 예측 충실도와 계획 성능에만 초점을 맞추고 조건부 행동에 대한 예측 의존성을 거의 확인하지 않는다는 점을 지적하며, 행동 조건부 의미론적 예측에서 행동 의존성을 연구합니다.
items.why_ko: 자율주행 AI의 의사결정 과정을 이해하고 개선하기 위해, 월드 모델이 실제 행동에 따라 예측을 얼마나 정확하게 조정하는지 평가하는 것은 시스템의 신뢰성을 높이는 데 필수적입니다.

items.title: Kaer: Security-Aware Replanning for Multi-Agent Systems
items.body:
One popular architecture for multi-agent systems (MAS) relies on an orchestrator that generates an initial plan, coordinates its execution, and dynamically revises the plan based on agent feedback when tasks cannot be fully specified in advance. This dynamic replanning introduces a critical vulnerability: malicious agents can embed instructions within their feedback to hijack the replanning process. Existing defenses focus exclusively on per-tool access control or static, pre-execution policy enforcement, leaving the replanning phase unsecured.
We introduce Kaer, a multi-agent framework featuring security-aware replanning. Kaer shields the planner from untrusted agent feedback by conveying diagnostics to the replanning procedure strictly through abstract templates. Plan revisions are restricted to a set of deterministic repair operators, and all modified plans must satisfy preset policies. We create Cintra, a benchmark of simulated user tasks requiring replanning paired with adversarial objectives targeting the replanning phase. Using Cintra, we evaluate both task completion rates and system vulnerability to replanning exploits by malicious agents. Evaluating Kaer on Cintra against Magentic-One (an undefended MAS) and ControlValve (the state-of-the-art defense) demonstrates that Kaer achieves higher robustness than both systems while maintaining comparable utility to ControlValve. Although abstract failure templates slightly constrain utility on select tasks, Kaer enables MAS to perform secure, dynamic plan revisions without exposing the orchestrator to untrusted agent feedback.
items.title_ko: Kaer: 다중 에이전트 시스템을 위한 보안 인식 재계획
items.summary_ko: 다중 에이전트 시스템(MAS)에서 오케스트레이터는 초기 계획을 생성하고 실행을 조율하며, 에이전트 피드백에 기반하여 동적으로 계획을 수정합니다. Kaer는 이러한 동적 재계획 과정에서 악성 에이전트가 피드백 내에 명령을 삽입하여 재계획 프로세스를 탈취할 수 있는 취약점을 해결하기 위한 보안 인식 재계획 방안을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트의 자율성과 유연성이 증가함에 따라 보안 취약점도 함께 증가하고 있습니다. Kaer는 다중 에이전트 시스템의 보안을 강화하는 실질적인 해결책을 제시하여 안전한 AI 시스템 개발에 기여합니다.

items.title: What Survival Benchmarks Don't Tell You: Impact of Model Selection and Dataset Regimes
items.body: Despite the proliferation of survival analysis methods, current benchmarks often operate under narrow conditions: they heavily rely on the concordance index (C-index) for evaluation and model selection, and frequently either exclude deep learning (DL) methods or underrepresent challenging dataset regimes. To address these limitations, we conduct a large-scale, neutral benchmark comparing 10 classical, tree-based, and DL methods across 49 diverse datasets. Crucially, we treat the model selection criterion (optimizing for C-index, Integrated Brier Score (IBS), or Mean Absolute Error (MAE-PO)) as an independent experimental variable. Using Bayesian mixed-effects modeling, we demonstrate that evaluation design heavily dictates conclusions. For complex DL and tree-based architectures, selecting hyperparameters to optimize for IBS instead of C-index yields substantial improvements in probabilistic accuracy and calibration at a negligible cost to discriminative ranking. Furthermore, method performance (C-index, IBS, MAE-PO, and X-CAL) is fundamentally governed by dataset characteristics. While DL models scale exceptionally well with larger sample sizes, they suffer notable performance drops in high-dimensional feature spaces. Additionally, we expose a structural vulnerability where heavy censoring artificially inflates absolute calibration metrics, creating overly conservative tests. Ultimately, our findings challenge the utility of global single-number performance summaries and advocate for survival analysis results that transparently report the evaluation setup. Our code is available at: https://github.com/sdening/surv-bench-study
items.title_ko: 생존 벤치마크가 알려주지 않는 것: 모델 선택 및 데이터셋 체제의 영향
items.summary_ko: 생존 분석 방법론의 확산에도 불구하고, 기존 벤치마크는 C-index 평가 및 모델 선택에 크게 의존하고 딥러닝 방법을 제외하거나 도전적인 데이터셋 체제를 과소대표하는 경향이 있습니다. 이 연구는 10가지 고전적, 트리 기반 및 딥러닝 방법을 49개 다양한 데이터셋에 걸쳐 비교하는 대규모 벤치마크를 수행합니다.
items.why_ko: 생존 분석 모델의 공정하고 포괄적인 평가는 의료 및 기타 고위험 분야에서 AI 모델의 신뢰성 확보에 필수적이며, 이 연구는 모델 선택과 데이터셋의 중요성을 강조합니다.

items.title: Overlooked and Underutilized: Prototypes are the Missing Piece in Tabular XAI
items.body: Explainable AI (XAI) is frequently applied to high-stakes tabular data, yet the field relies heavily on feature attribution methods. While these approaches offer technical transparency, evaluating dozens of isolated features demands excessive cognitive effort from non-expert users. In this paper, we argue that prototypes remain overlooked and underutilized, and should be integrated as a complementary, intuitive gateway to auditing complex machine learning models. Although entire exemplars function as an intuitive baseline for prototype-based explanations, we highlight prototypical parts as particularly valuable for tabular data. By grouping related features into bounded subspaces, prototypical parts technically embody human-understandable concepts, replacing isolated features with cohesive semantic units. We support this integration through two primary lenses. Cognitively, these parts align with Rosch's categorization theory and Kahneman's System 1 thinking to naturally reduce cognitive load for humans. Then, we introduce a Geometric Validity Triad to conceptualize why prototypes validate the data manifold - a critical dimension often neglected by existing methods. We contend that making tabular XAI genuinely comprehensible requires shifting toward composite explanation pipelines that pair intuitive similarity-based reasoning with rigorous feature-level auditing. The paper concludes by outlining open challenges of prototype-based methods and discussing potential solutions to guide future research.
items.title_ko: 간과되고 저활용된 것: 프로토타입은 테이블 XAI의 누락된 조각이다
items.summary_ko: 설명 가능한 AI(XAI)는 고위험 테이블 데이터에 자주 적용되지만, 주로 특징 기여도 방법에 의존합니다. 이 연구는 프로토타입이 간과되고 저활용되었다고 주장하며, 복잡한 머신러닝 모델을 감사하는 직관적인 관문으로서 프로토타입의 통합을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: XAI의 해석 가능성을 높이는 것은 AI 시스템의 신뢰성을 확보하는 데 중요합니다. 프로토타입 기반 설명은 비전문가 사용자도 AI 모델의 결정을 더 쉽게 이해하도록 도와줍니다.

items.title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to infer psychological attributes, predict individual behaviour, and simulate human populations. However, despite generating plausible responses, they often misrepresent individuals and distort population statistics. Here we introduce Chiron, a foundation model to measure and predict human behaviour. We jointly fine-tune an LLM to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align population response distributions with human statistics. The training and evaluation data span 36 behavioural domains and 78 social science experiments, comprising 288,307 person records, 1,411,750 atomic behavioural decisions, and 99,953 psychometric assessments over 109 psychological constructs. In our evaluations, Chiron's psychological measurements agree more closely with human self-reports and exhibit fewer biases that undermine psychometric validity. It predicts individual behaviour more accurately than frontier LLMs (up to 28.4% relative improvement). In simulations of social science experiments, it more accurately captures the direction and magnitude of human experimental effects (82.2--94.3% lower effect-size estimation error). Together, these results establish Chiron as a unified computational instrument for measuring and predicting human behaviour.
items.title_ko: 인간 행동 측정 및 예측을 위한 파운데이션 모델
items.summary_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)이 심리적 속성 추론, 개인 행동 예측, 인간 집단 시뮬레이션에 사용되지만, 종종 개인을 잘못 나타내거나 집단 통계를 왜곡합니다. 이 연구는 심리적 구성 개념을 표현하고, 개인 행동을 예측하며, 집단 응답 분포를 인간과 정렬하도록 LLM을 공동 미세 조정하는 파운데이션 모델 Chiron을 소개합니다.
items.why_ko: 인간 행동을 정확하게 모델링하는 것은 사회 과학, 의료 및 개인화 서비스 분야에서 AI의 응용 가능성을 확장하며, LLM의 한계를 극복하고 신뢰도를 높이는 데 중요합니다.

items.title: Synthesizing hyperspectral Data using generative Models to train spectral Unmixing Methods for low-cost Crop Residue Cover Mapping
items.body: The spectral range of the Field Imaging Nanosatellite for Crop residue Hyperspectral Mapping (FINCH), developed by the University of Toronto Aerospace Team's Space System Division, poses significant challenges for hyperspectral unmixing to determine crop residue cover fractional abundances. The severe lack of standard indices necessitates the use of complex, data-driven unmixing models. Complex unmixing models require dense, well-distributed manifolds, whereas ground-truth datasets are sparse and expensive. To better leverage the information content in existing ground-truth datasets, this study presents a framework that decouples interpolation and abundance-mapping estimation via an intermediary conditional data generator, contrasting with traditional single-model unmixing pipelines. This decoupling enables the inclusion of physical prior knowledge about spectra, which is not natively accessible to unmixing models, thereby artificially expanding the dataset to serve as a Monte Carlo approximation of the population risk. To test this hypothesis, we have proposed two generator models: a 1D Conditional U-Net with Conformer Layers (GD-Streamline) and a Dual-Path Transformer Conditional Variational AutoEncoder (TCVAE), and two unmixing models: Multi-Layered Perceptrons (MLP) and Fourier Neural Operators (FNO). The results of the study indicate a need for rigorous integration and introduction of spectral priors within the scope of the proposed decoupling framework to prevent domain and mode collapse and hallucination by the generator models; otherwise, this leads to falsely approximated data manifolds, ultimately resulting in unsatisfactory and out-of-distribution unmixing performance.
items.title_ko: 저비용 작물 잔류물 커버 매핑을 위한 스펙트럼 언믹싱 방법 훈련을 위한 생성 모델을 사용한 초분광 데이터 합성
items.summary_ko: 작물 잔류물 커버 분수 풍부도를 결정하기 위한 초분광 언믹싱 방법 훈련을 위해 생성 모델을 사용하여 초분광 데이터를 합성하는 연구입니다. FINCH(Field Imaging Nanosatellite for Crop residue Hyperspectral Mapping)의 스펙트럼 범위가 복잡한 데이터 기반 언믹싱 모델을 요구하지만, 지상 실측 데이터가 희박하다는 문제를 해결하고자 합니다.
items.why_ko: 농업 분야에서 AI를 활용한 정밀 모니터링은 중요하지만, 개발자에게 직접적인 실무 지식을 제공하지는 않습니다.

items.title: LAaDT-DSS: decision support for non-experts on rooftop PV, incentive and grid simulations under Turkish tariff rules
items.body: Rooftop photovoltaics raise three questions: should a household invest, which incentive costs the state least, and does the feeder stay within limits? Those who ask are rarely modellers. We present LAaDT-DSS, decision-support software that answers all three under Turkish tariff rules from one simulation core. Non-experts reach it by clicking a house on a 3D map or by asking in plain words; a language model is asked to call the simulation tools, not to compute. Each entry of its 125-entry parameter registry is marked as sourced or estimated. Case studies test the system. Its PV yield lies within $\pm$3.6% of two independent tools at equal losses. Across 2,048 draws of its estimated inputs, the answer for PV alone held in all but one; with a battery, it changed in 31-41% of the draws. Four scripted chat scenarios ran end to end; no user study was run.
items.title_ko: LAaDT-DSS: 터키 요금 규정에 따른 옥상 태양광, 인센티브 및 그리드 시뮬레이션 비전문가용 의사결정 지원 시스템
items.summary_ko: LAaDT-DSS는 옥상 태양광 투자, 국가 인센티브, 그리드 제한에 대한 비전문가용 의사결정 지원 소프트웨어입니다. 언어 모델을 사용하여 시뮬레이션 도구를 호출하고, 단일 시뮬레이션 코어를 통해 터키 요금 규정 하에서 세 가지 질문에 모두 답변합니다.
items.why_ko: AI를 활용하여 복잡한 의사결정 과정을 비전문가도 쉽게 접근할 수 있도록 돕는 시스템으로, 실제 문제 해결에 AI를 적용하는 좋은 사례입니다.

items.title: On-Policy Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models
items.body: Hybrid attention models combine full and linear attention to achieve a better quality--efficiency trade-off. Converting pretrained Transformers into such models requires identifying which layers should retain full attention under a prescribed budget. We identify two off-policy mismatches in FlashMorph's layer selection: (i) continuous branch interpolation and teacher-forced hidden states differ from discrete hybrid computation; and (ii) frozen model weights fail to account for parameter adaptation during subsequent recovery. We introduce FlashMorph2, an on-policy layer-selection method that (I) evaluates sampled discrete hybrid architectures end to end using their own hidden states, and (II) jointly optimizes layer-selection scores and model weights under the recovery objective to reflect post-adaptation performance. Experiments across Qwen3 model scales and linear-attention variants show that FlashMorph2 consistently outperforms existing layer-selection methods, improving average scores over FlashMorph by $+2.42$ points on RULER, $+1.08$ on LongBench, and $+0.76$ on recall-intensive tasks, while completing layer selection in only $0.72$--$3.57$ GPU hours across 0.6B--8B models, demonstrating high efficiency and scalability.
items.title_ko: On-Policy Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models
items.summary_ko: 하이브리드 어텐션 모델은 완전 어텐션과 선형 어텐션을 결합하여 더 나은 품질-효율성 절충을 달성합니다. 사전 훈련된 트랜스포머를 이러한 모델로 변환하려면 주어진 예산 내에서 어떤 계층이 완전 어텐션을 유지해야 하는지 식별해야 합니다.
items.why_ko: 트랜스포머 기반 모델의 효율성과 성능을 개선하는 것은 LLM 개발의 핵심 과제이며, 하이브리드 어텐션 모델로의 전환은 실용적인 최적화 기법을 제공할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Prognosis Without Prediction: The Intrinsic Geometry of Survival
items.body: Modeling systemic failure in high-dimensional environments is fundamentally limited by supervised algorithms that attempt to predict sparse, noisy or censored endpoints. To break this reliance on explicit outcome regression, we engineered the Self-Organizing Survival Manifolds (SOSM) framework, a deep learning architecture that decouples unsupervised representation learning from survival labels and treats time-to-event progression as an emergent geometric property. The system projects heterogeneous multi-omics arrays into a unified latent space governed by a pseudotime-weighted, curvature-minimizing graph Laplacian, organizing patient trajectories along low-dissipation geodesic flows. To validate the framework, we applied this architecture to a 184-patient clear cell renal cell carcinoma multi-omics cohort. Across a deterministic 5-fold cross-validation pipeline, SOSM achieved a mean Concordance Index of $0.768 \pm 0.068$, while out-of-fold risk stratification yielded significant survival divergence (log-rank $p < 0.001$) accompanied by a 14.7% increase in local manifold dissipation among high-risk patients. Furthermore, interrogating the network's encoder weights confirmed that the model autonomously recovered canonical metabolic and microenvironmental drivers of disease progression without supervised feature selection. By demonstrating that systemic failure can be mapped as a geometric phase transition, SOSM establishes a generalizable computational engine for prognostic modeling across biological, industrial and financial complex systems.
items.title_ko: 예측 없는 예후: 생존의 내재적 기하학
items.summary_ko: 고차원 환경에서 시스템 실패를 모델링하는 것은 희소하고 노이즈가 많거나 censored된 종말점을 예측하려는 지도 알고리즘에 의해 근본적으로 제한됩니다. 이 연구는 지도 학습의 이러한 의존성을 깨기 위해, 비지도 표현 학습을 생존 레이블과 분리하고 시간-이벤트 진행을 발생하는 기하학적 속성으로 처리하는 SOSM(Self-Organizing Survival Manifolds) 프레임워크를 개발했습니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 및 신뢰성 공학 분야에서 중요한 생존 분석의 한계를 극복하고, 고차원 데이터에서 시간-이벤트 예측의 정확도를 높일 수 있는 새로운 딥러닝 아키텍처를 제시합니다.

items.title: Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Learning
items.body: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has attracted increasing interest as a possible route to construct feature representations that are difficult to reproduce with classical models.
